prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Pasadena, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1029; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision at the intersection in Pasadena, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just leave my name out of it, if that's okay. The collision is what matters, right?

Q: That's fine for the transcript. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving through the intersection on a green light, heading straight through. The other car came in from the cross street on my right side.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before impact?

A: Not really. I glanced left, saw nothing coming, and then it was right there. I braked, but there wasn't time.

Q: How fast do you estimate you were traveling?

A: Maybe thirty-five, close to the speed limit. I wasn't speeding.

Q: Was anyone else in your vehicle?

A: No, I was alone.

Q: Can you tell me about your injuries?

A: My left wrist took the worst of it. I put my arm out against the door and the steering wheel when the car spun. The doctor says it's a fracture. I've got a cast and I'm supposed to see a specialist next week.

Q: Did you receive medical treatment at the scene or afterward?

A: An ambulance took me from the scene to the emergency room. They X-rayed the wrist and set it, then sent me home with instructions.

Q: Is there anything you'd like to add about how the collision happened?

A: Only that the other driver's car came out of nowhere. I was following the signal and doing what I was supposed to do.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.

A: Okay, thanks.
